title: SQL constraint types and schema evolution
summary: Implement named PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK, and default rules.
intro: SQL constraint syntax turns integrity requirements into database objects. Naming and testing those objects makes a schema easier to diagnose and evolve than a collection of undocumented assumptions.
outcomes: Plan a constraint change without ignoring existing data.

sections.title: 1. Match each requirement to its mechanism
paragraphs: PRIMARY KEY gives the designated required identity. UNIQUE enforces an alternative uniqueness rule. FOREIGN KEY validates references. NOT NULL requires a present value. CHECK rejects rows whose predicate is FALSE. DEFAULT supplies a value when the column is omitted or DEFAULT is requested; it is not a substitute for a constraint.

table.caption: Constraint choices
rows: One designated key; may be composite

sections.title: 2. A named constraint is a diagnosable rule
paragraphs: Table-level syntax is convenient for composite keys and named relationships. Column-level syntax can express simple rules. Use explicit table-level FOREIGN KEY clauses for portable teaching scripts rather than relying on inline REFERENCES forms that some engine versions ignore.
sections.code:
CREATE TABLE U3RegistrationRule (
  registration_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  student_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reference_code VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  status VARCHAR(12) DEFAULT 'pending' NOT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT u3_rule_pk PRIMARY KEY (registration_id),
  CONSTRAINT u3_rule_ref_uq UNIQUE (reference_code),
  CONSTRAINT u3_rule_student_fk FOREIGN KEY (student_id)
    REFERENCES U3Student(student_id),
  CONSTRAINT u3_rule_status_ck CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'confirmed'))
);
INSERT INTO U3RegistrationRule (registration_id, student_id, reference_code)
VALUES (1, 101, 'R-101');
SELECT registration_id, status FROM U3RegistrationRule;

example: The INSERT omits status, so the default produces pending. Explicit status = NULL would fail NOT NULL; status = 'finished' would fail CHECK; reference_code = 'R-101' on a second row would fail UNIQUE. Each error identifies a different broken rule.

sections.title: 3. Key and NULL portability traps
paragraphs: A PRIMARY KEY expresses both uniqueness and required identity, but SQLite has historical behaviours for some non-integer primary-key definitions. The shared fixture uses explicit NOT NULL key columns so the exercise does not rely on that exception.

UNIQUE with nullable columns has different NULL policies across engines and index options. For a portable required unique reference, declare both UNIQUE and NOT NULL. Do not claim that every product permits unlimited NULLs or exactly one NULL in a unique column.

sections.title: 4. Add a constraint as a data migration
paragraphs: A new rule must be checked against existing rows. Before requiring email, find NULL emails; Ravi is a known counterexample. Decide whether to collect the value, retain optionality, or redesign the rule. Inventing placeholder emails to satisfy a migration corrupts the meaning of the data.

ALTER TABLE syntax, validation options, lock behaviour, and online facilities vary. SQLite often requires a table-rebuild migration for constraint changes that other engines express directly. Design and test the migration for its real server instead of presenting one ALTER statement as universal.

sections.title: 5. Choose a constraint before a trigger
paragraphs: Declarative keys and checks describe invariants directly and integrate with the engine. A trigger adds hidden execution paths and may require concurrency reasoning. Prefer a simple CHECK to a trigger that merely rejects mark > 100, and prefer a foreign key to a trigger that looks for a parent.

Test both acceptance and rejection: pending and confirmed are valid; NULL and unrecognized status are invalid; a duplicate reference fails; an unknown student fails. A success-path insert alone does not establish that the schema enforces its intended boundary.

revision: Name constraints and distinguish defaults from rejection rules.
Test composite identity, alternative uniqueness, required values, and references.
Inspect existing rows before adding a stricter rule.

questions.question: Does DEFAULT pending prevent any other status?
answer: No. DEFAULT supplies an omitted value. CHECK restricts the permitted status set, and NOT NULL prevents an explicitly missing value. All three serve different purposes.

questions.question: Why combine UNIQUE and NOT NULL on reference_code?
answer: The reference is both required and nonduplicated. UNIQUE alone does not consistently enforce requiredness across products because NULL handling varies.

questions.question: Can a NOT NULL migration succeed on the baseline email column?
answer: Not while Ravi's email remains NULL. First inspect and resolve the policy for existing rows. Changing constraints without a data plan may fail, block work, or encourage incorrect placeholder values.
